summary: E2E tested admin 'Login As User' (impersonation) flow after duplicate /api/admin/impersonate/{target_uid} endpoint was removed from server.py. Admin login -> Admin Dashboard -> Login As User dialog -> search mobile 9970100782 -> select SANTOSH AVHALE -> submit WITHOUT PIN -> POST /api/admin/login-as-user returns 200 with IMP_ token and correct user. Admin session is restored in original tab after 300ms, paras_impersonation flag is cleared, duplicate endpoint regression verified (not present in server.py / admin_misc.py). However, a real race condition was reproduced: the new impersonation tab opened but displayed the admin's own identity because the 300ms setTimeout restored the admin's localStorage BEFORE the new tab finished loading the React app in the automated browser — new tab ended up at /login with admin UID 'admin-test-123' / name 'Test Admin' instead of SANTOSH.

ui_bugs.issue: 'Login As User' button lacks data-testid; also no data-testid on the dialog/search input/confirm/login-as-user submit button — making automation fragile.
ui_bugs.selector: button:has-text('Login As User'), [role=dialog] input[placeholder='Enter Mobile, Name or Email...']

ui_bugs.issue: React warning: 'Each child in a list should have a unique key prop. Check the render method of AdminDashboard.' Not blocking but should be fixed.

integration_issues.issue: Race condition: AdminLoginAsUser.js writes impersonation data to localStorage, window.open('/dashboard','_blank'), then setTimeout(300ms) restores admin session. In automation (and any slow/cold new-tab load), the new tab reads localStorage AFTER admin restore and mounts as admin, not the impersonated user. Reproduced consistently in Playwright: new tab URL ended at /login with paras_user={name:'Test Admin', uid:'admin-test-123'} instead of SANTOSH AVHALE. Recommend passing session_token via URL hash (e.g. /dashboard#imp=<token>) or via postMessage to the new window, or dedicated /impersonate-landing route that pulls from sessionStorage keyed by a nonce.

action_items: Fix race condition in AdminLoginAsUser.js: instead of writing paras_user+restoring in 300ms, pass the impersonation session_token to the new tab via URL hash/query (e.g. window.open(`/dashboard#imp=${session_token}`)) and have App.js hydrate from the hash. This removes timing fragility entirely.
Add data-testid attributes: admin-login-as-user-btn (dashboard), impersonation-search-input, impersonation-result-<uid>, impersonation-confirm-login-btn.
Resolve React 'unique key prop' warning in AdminDashboard render (list without keys).
critical_code_review_comments: AdminLoginAsUser.js relies on a 300ms window to restore admin session in the opener tab while the opened tab reads localStorage on mount. This is inherently racy — browsers/devices under load, backgrounded tabs, popup defer, or cold-start SW revalidation can all cause the new tab to finish hydrating after 300ms, at which point it reads the RESTORED admin user. Use a per-handoff token in URL instead.

admin_pin is accepted as optional by the backend (login-as-user 200 with empty pin). If this is intentional (per requirement), fine — but label UI 'Admin PIN (Optional)' is accurate. Consider a rate limit or audit log per impersonation event (partially present: 'impersonated_by_admin' field at admin_misc.py:756).
Dialog uses loose text selectors — adding data-testid would make this feature testable in regression runs.

Popup opens but empties to /login because of race condition.
rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE of new-tab issue: In AdminLoginAsUser.js#loginAsUser (lines 85-101), the component: (1) saves admin's current localStorage.paras_user to a variable, (2) overwrites paras_user with impersonation data, (3) calls window.open('/dashboard','_blank'), (4) schedules a 300ms setTimeout to restore admin's paras_user. The new tab reads localStorage on React mount to determine which user to hydrate. In any slower scenario (automation, cold start, backgrounded tab, slow CPU), mount happens >300ms after window.open, so the new tab reads the already-restored admin data and mounts as admin (then redirects to /login because the admin's token may already be stale or the canAccessAdmin router pushes admin to /admin not /dashboard). MITIGATION: encode session_token in the URL hash (window.open(`/dashboard#imp=${encodeURIComponent(session_token)}`)) and have App.js initialization check window.location.hash for `imp=` before reading localStorage; this removes the shared mutable localStorage handoff entirely. Alternative: use sessionStorage (per-tab) rather than localStorage (shared).
